newsitem.title: USA: Missouri fields begin to dry out after wet winter.
newsitem.headline: Missouri fields begin to dry out after wet winter.

text.p: Below normal precipitation in March allowed many areas of Missouri to begin to dry out from the extremely wet winter months, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.

But wet weather continued in the Bootheel, limiting fieldwork in the area. Farmers there were anxious to begin corn planting while producers further north focused on preparations such as tillage and fertilizer applications.
Winter wheat was rated nine percent poor, 29 percent fair, 52 percent good and 10 percent excellent, improved from a month earlier.
Thirty-eight percent of the oat crop had been sown, compared with 39 percent last year and an average 34 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated three percent short, 74 percent adequate and 23 percent surplus. No districts were reporting significant moisture shortages.
Thirty-nine percent of the ground had been worked at least once for spring crops, compared with 46 percent last year and 41 percent on average.
"Some areas of the state which have been hampered by a wet winter are still waiting for additional dry weather before beginning tillage operations," the report said.
